misconceptions.description: Uses nd instead of (n − 1)d in AP formulas.
misconceptions.remediation: The first term already counts as term 1, so the nth term is a + (n − 1)d. Check with n = 1: you must get a.
(α + β)² = α² + β² + 2αβ. So α² + β² = (α + β)² − 2αβ. Expand the square fully every time.

misconceptions.description: Makes a sign error in integration by parts.
misconceptions.remediation: ∫u dv = uv − ∫v du. Write the minus sign before the second integral as the very first thing, then evaluate it.

misconceptions.description: Counts arrangements of repeated letters as if all letters were distinct.
misconceptions.remediation: With repeated items, divide by the factorial of each repeat count: n!/(p! q! …). List a tiny case (e.g. 'AAB') to convince yourself.

misconceptions.description: Reads the centre of x² + y² + 2gx + 2fy + c = 0 as (g, f) instead of (−g, −f).
misconceptions.remediation: Complete the squares: (x + g)² + (y + f)² = g² + f² − c. The centre is where each bracket is zero, i.e. (−g, −f).

misconceptions.description: Uses |kA| = k|A| for an n×n matrix.
misconceptions.remediation: Multiplying the matrix by k multiplies *every row* by k, so |kA| = kⁿ|A| for an n×n matrix.

misconceptions.description: Counts unordered outcomes when the sample space is ordered.
misconceptions.remediation: Two dice are distinguishable, so (1,6) and (6,1) are different outcomes out of 36. Keep numerator and denominator in the same (ordered) space.

misconceptions.description: Cancels sin⁻¹(sin x) = x without checking the principal range.
misconceptions.remediation: sin⁻¹ always returns a value in [−π/2, π/2]. First rewrite the angle inside as an equivalent one in that range with the same sine.
